$comment: Condition vectors per spec/04-expression-language.md#conditions. Each case evaluates one path against `document`, compares against one literal, using exactly one of the five operators. No boolean composition exists in this language, so every case is a single comparison.

cases.description: == true case
== false case
!= true case
!= false case
> true case, numeric
> false case, numeric
> false case, equal values
< true case, numeric
< false case, numeric
in true case, literal list
in false case, literal list
comparison against a value from a wildcard-projected array is not supported by this language; conditions read one scalar path, never a projection
missing path never equals any literal, including the empty string
missing path is never `in` any list, including one containing an empty string
< false case, equal values (symmetric with the > equal-values case above)
!= on a missing path is true: a missing value never equals any literal, so it is unequal to all of them, including its complement of the == false-case for the empty string above
> on a missing path is false, not an error: comparison against an unresolved path is never true for any operator
< on a missing path is false for the same reason
== never coerces type: a numeric field is never equal to the same digits as a string literal
== never coerces type in the other direction either: a string field is never equal to the same digits as a numeric literal
== on a boolean field against a boolean literal
== never coerces a boolean field against a string literal, even "true"
in with a single-element list
in does not coerce type: a numeric field is never `in` a list of the same digits as strings
in with an empty literal list is always false, for any field
